newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - Time Warner cash flow rises in Q4.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Time Warner cash flow rises in Q4.

text.p: Time Warner Inc on Tuesday posted strong fourth-quarter results, buoyed by higher operating cash flow in nearly every one of its divisions. The company also forecast a strong 1997 performance, suggesting it would show record results for the year.

Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization rose in Time Warner's publishing, cable television and film divisions. One of the few weak links -- the music division -- mirrored a lackluster showing by the rest of that industry, analysts said.
Time Warner's stock closed up about 1-7/8 to 41-1/2.

Several analysts said they were encouraged by the nominations of Hilton Hotels Corp Chief Executive Stephen Bollenbach and UAL Corp Chairman Gerald Greenwald to Time Warner's board of directors. Bollenbach and Greenwald are viewed as aggressive business leaders who have experience in restructurings.

Bollenbach, who was chief financial officer of Walt Disney Co during its successful bid for Capital Cities/ABC, is seen as a takeover specialist who could help Time Warner in the aftermath of its merger with Turner Broadcasting Systems. Hilton is currently making a bid for ITT Corp.
